title: SOC 2 Evidence Sharing Playbook (Under NDA) — Redwood Inference
content:
RESTRICTED / INTERNAL ONLY

Document purpose
- This playbook standardizes how Redwood Inference shares SOC 2 evidence with prospects/customers during security review.
- Goals: consistent messaging, correct handling under NDA, fast turnaround, and clear audit trail of what we shared with whom.
- Audience: GRC/Compliance, Security PM, Solutions Engineering, Sales (AE/SE) when coordinating requests.

Scope
Included
- SOC 2 Type II report sharing process (under NDA)
- Common evidence requests: bridge letter (if applicable), management assertion, description of system, pen test summary (high-level), policy excerpts (select), subprocessor list pointer
- Email templates + approval checklist
- Tracking + storage conventions

Not included
- Legal contract redlines (route to Legal/Finance)
- “Custom attestation letters” (case-by-case; route to GRC lead + Legal)
- Sharing raw pen test report / vulnerability details (not shared externally unless explicitly approved by Security Eng + CISO)

Hard rules (do not deviate)
1) No SOC 2 report is shared without an executed NDA (or MSA/DPA that includes confidentiality terms acceptable to Legal).
2) Share only the most current approved artifacts from the designated source folder(s). Do not forward older PDFs from email.
3) Use the approved email templates below. Do not paraphrase claims about scope, exceptions, or timelines.
4) Record the share in the Evidence Distribution Log the same day.
5) If the requester asks for anything outside this playbook, pause and escalate to GRC + Security Eng.

Primary owners
- GRC owner / final approver for SOC 2 evidence sharing: Olga Petrov
- Evidence coordinator (packaging + log): Daniel Carter
- Escalations:
  - Security scope/technical questions: Marcus Lin
  - Customer-facing claim wording: Naomi Feldman
  - Exceptions / high-risk accounts: Dr. Aisha Rahman
  - Deal coordination: AE/SE owner + Markus Klein as needed

Turnaround targets (operational)
- Standard SOC 2 report request (NDA already executed): 1 business day
- NDA not yet executed: 2–5 business days depending on customer turnaround
- Non-standard evidence request: acknowledge within 1 business day, provide ETA after triage

Definitions
- “SOC 2 report” = auditor’s SOC 2 Type II report (restricted distribution; NDA required)
- “SOC 2 letter of attestation/bridge letter” = optional supplemental letter for a coverage period gap (only if available and approved for distribution)
- “Evidence” = any document that describes controls, testing results, or security posture beyond our public docs

Where the truth lives (source locations)
NOTE: Do not paste these links into external emails. Share via approved methods only.
- Canonical internal process: Confluence → security-and-compliance/compliance-evidence/customer-security-review-process
- Approved customer-facing summaries (safe to share without NDA):
  - Confluence → sales-enablement/security-faq/enterprise-security-faq-v2
  - One-pagers pack (encryption, audit logs, retention/residency, SSO/RBAC)
- Internal evidence index: Linear ENG-23344 (pointer list + locations)

What we can share (and under what conditions)
A) Shareable WITHOUT NDA (customer-facing / marketing-safe)
- Security FAQ v2 PDF (field-ready)
- One-pagers pack v2 (SOC 2 posture summary slide, encryption, SSO/RBAC, audit logging overview, data residency + retention)
- Public security overview docs pages (if referenced by prospect)

B) Shareable ONLY WITH NDA
- SOC 2 Type II report (current period)
- SOC 2 bridge letter (if applicable)
- Select policy excerpts (only from the approved “external excerpt” versions)

C) Not shareable by default (requires explicit approval)
- Full penetration test report
- Detailed vulnerability reports or scanner outputs
- Security architecture diagrams that expose internal segmentation, tooling, or sensitive details
- Customer-specific control mappings (can be created, but treat as restricted and route for review)

Intake process (end-to-end)
1) Request arrives
- Typical sources: AE/SE email, security questionnaire, customer security portal upload request, or support ticket.
- Required intake fields (collect before proceeding):
  - Company name + domain
  - Deal stage / renewal vs net-new
  - Customer contact name + corporate email
  - Is NDA executed? If yes, what covers it (NDA/MSA) and effective date
  - What exactly is being requested (SOC 2 report vs “proof of SOC 2” vs bridge letter)
  - Deadline + security review meeting date

2) Confirm NDA status
- If NDA exists: verify via Sales/Legal record (or ask AE to provide executed copy or confirmation from Legal).
- If NDA does not exist: route NDA initiation to AE + Legal; do not share restricted evidence.

3) Determine the artifact set
Default (most requests)
- SOC 2 Type II report (latest)
Optional (only if asked or needed)
- Bridge letter (if there’s a period gap concern)
- Subprocessor list pointer (customer-facing) + DPA request routing
- High-level pen test summary (if approved)

4) Approvals
- Standard SOC 2 report share: GRC owner approval (Olga) OR delegated approval to Daniel Carter if explicitly delegated for the quarter.
- Non-standard artifacts: GRC + Security Eng approval; CISO approval for high-risk exceptions.

5) Sharing method (approved)
- Preferred: secure file share link with access control (time-bound link where possible) OR customer’s security portal upload by GRC.
- If email attachment is unavoidable: password-protect the PDF and share the password via separate channel (never in same email thread). Confirm the recipient’s corporate email.
- Do not share via personal emails, Slack Connect, or unapproved link-sharing settings.

6) Recordkeeping
- Log the distribution in Evidence Distribution Log (same day): who requested, who approved, what was shared, date, and method.
- Store the executed NDA location pointer (do not duplicate legal docs into random folders).

Approval checklist (copy/paste)
Requester + context
[ ] Requester is a customer/prospect with corporate email
[ ] Company name + domain confirmed
[ ] Deal context recorded (net-new/renewal; region)

NDA verification
[ ] Executed NDA / confidentiality coverage verified (date + doc type)
[ ] NDA covers sharing third-party audit report
[ ] If portal requires click-through terms, reviewed/approved by Legal (or explicitly allowed)

Artifact verification
[ ] Using the latest approved SOC 2 report (correct period)
[ ] Artifact is unmodified (no screenshots / no partial pages)
[ ] Any optional artifacts included are approved for external distribution

Security + distribution
[ ] Sharing method uses access controls (restricted recipients)
[ ] Link settings verified (no “anyone with link”)
[ ] If attachment: password-protected and password shared separately

Logging
[ ] Evidence Distribution Log entry created/updated
[ ] Any special conditions (expiry date, portal upload, customer name mismatch) noted

Email templates

Template 1 — NDA required (initial response)
Subject: SOC 2 Report Request — NDA Required

Hi {Name},

Thanks for the request. We can provide our SOC 2 Type II report under NDA (or under the confidentiality terms of an existing agreement).

To proceed, please confirm whether an NDA/MSA is already in place between {Customer} and Redwood Inference. If it is, please share the effective date and contracting entity name (or have your procurement/legal team confirm).

If not, we can route an NDA for signature and share the report once executed.

In the meantime, we can share our customer-facing security materials (Security FAQ and security/compliance one-pagers) if helpful.

Best regards,
{Sender Name}
Security & Compliance (GRC)
security@redwoodinference.com

Template 2 — NDA confirmed (share evidence)
Subject: SOC 2 Type II Report — Redwood Inference (Under NDA)

Hi {Name},

As confirmed, the SOC 2 Type II report is being shared under the NDA/confidentiality terms in place between {Customer Legal Entity} and Redwood Inference.

Access instructions:
- {Link to secure share OR portal upload confirmation}
- Notes: Please treat this report as Confidential and limit distribution to individuals involved in your security/compliance review.

If your team has questions about the report scope, system boundaries, or how it relates to your deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), we can schedule time with our Security team and Solutions Engineering.

Best regards,
{Sender Name}
Security & Compliance (GRC)

Template 3 — Bridge letter request (if applicable)
Subject: SOC 2 Bridge Letter Request — Redwood Inference

Hi {Name},

We understand the request for a bridge letter to address the period between audit coverage dates. We’re confirming availability and approval for external distribution.

We’ll follow up with an ETA once confirmed. In the meantime, the SOC 2 Type II report (under NDA) remains the primary evidence of our control environment for the audited period.

Best regards,
{Sender Name}
Security & Compliance (GRC)

Template 4 — Decline / escalate non-standard evidence request
Subject: Re: Security Evidence Request

Hi {Name},

Thanks for outlining the request. Some of the items you asked for are not part of our standard evidence package and require additional review before we can share.

We’re routing this internally with our Security and Compliance teams and will come back with what we can provide and an ETA.

Best regards,
{Sender Name}

Common tricky scenarios + guidance
1) Customer asks: “Can you confirm you’re SOC 2 certified?”
- Use: “Redwood Inference has completed a SOC 2 Type II audit.”
- Avoid: “Certified” (SOC 2 is an attestation report, not a certification).

2) Customer wants SOC 2 report sent to a personal email
- Decline and request a corporate email, or route through their security portal if approved.

3) Customer security portal requires accepting portal T&Cs
- If T&Cs are standard and previously approved, proceed; otherwise route to Legal (do not click-accept on behalf of Redwood without approval).

4) “Just send me a screenshot of the exceptions section”
- Do not do this. Share the full report via approved method under NDA.

5) Customer requests the SOC 2 report AND pen test report
- SOC 2: proceed under NDA.
- Pen test: default is no; offer the approved pen test summary (if available) or schedule a call to discuss program approach. Escalate to Marcus/Naomi.

6) EMEA / data residency concerns
- Provide the data residency one-pager (no NDA required) and clarify deployment mode boundaries. If they require evidence tied to specific regions, route to GRC for controlled response.

Evidence Distribution Log (minimum fields)
- Date shared
- Company
- Recipient name + email
- NDA status (verified; date)
- Artifact(s) shared (SOC 2 report period; bridge letter yes/no)
- Sharing method (secure link / portal upload / password-protected attachment)
- Approver (name)
- Notes (special conditions, expiry, portal name)
